patches: column-lists.js — `_constraint_literal` accepts CONSTRAINT <name> UNIQUE | FOREIGN KEY | INDEX. Measured on the shipped build: `CONSTRAINT uq UNIQUE (b)` and `CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY (b) REFERENCES o (a)` each produced an ERROR and the constraint NAME was lost, while the unnamed forms parsed — so the gap only ever showed on named constraints, which is the common case in a real schema.
delete.js — `DELETE FROM t AS x` and `DELETE FROM t USING o`; both produced an ERROR and the USING table's edge was lost.

grant.js (new) — visible `grant_statement` / `revoke_statement`. The shipped build had no `grant`/`revoke`/`keyword_grant` token at all, so `GRANT SELECT ON t TO joe` was 2 ERROR nodes and `REVOKE … FROM joe` put the ROLE name where the analyzer read a table.
do-drop-policy.js (new) — `do_statement` and `drop_policy`. `keyword_do` existed but was wired only to MySQL's ON DUPLICATE KEY DO UPDATE; `DO $$ … $$` was 3 ERROR nodes.

create.js — `index_fields` left MANDATORY. `optional($.index_fields)` was tried so `CREATE INDEX ix ON t;` (no key list) would parse; it leaves an unresolved LR conflict on `… object_reference • '('` inside while_statement and `generate` refuses outright. A column-less index is invalid SQL in every major dialect, so the shape stays a documented gap rather than trading a working grammar for it.
grammar_provenance.removed_after_measurement: An opaque whole-`$$ … $$` token alternative was added to `function_body` and `procedure_body` and then REMOVED as inert. `externals` declares `$._dollar_quoted_string` and the scanner can consume a whole body as one token, but only when the START TAG is not simultaneously valid — scanner.c tests `valid_symbols[DOLLAR_QUOTED_STRING_START_TAG]` first and returns whenever `state->start_tag == NULL`. Offering both forms in one `choice` makes the opaque branch unreachable. Measured across five shapes: every `dollar_quote` node was the bare two-character tag, opaque (body-spanning) count 0 of 10. The same reasoning is why `do_statement` IS opaque-only — with no structured alternative competing for the tag, the token becomes reachable and a `DO` body is arbitrary PL/pgSQL anyway, so nothing is lost. The cascade-recovery improvement in the corpus is attributable to the OTHER rules above plus the analyzer's own declaration sweep and resync, each measured separately — an earlier revision of the patch wrongly credited the opaque branch, and that credit is withdrawn here.

grammar_provenance.adjudicated_f11_reading: F11 reports the candidate INADMISSIBLE, and each of its three verdicts was adjudicated against the trees rather than accepted at face value. G1: 2 newly-damaged files against fixed 34 / improved 146 / worse 21. G2: 5 files clean under the pinned grammar change shape, and all 5 GAIN a `having` node the pinned build dropped (e.g. `HAVING COUNT(p.policyname) = 0`). G3: −177 symbols / −441 pairs against +1813 / +2156, and 138 of the 177 are `property:ENABLE` — the pinned grammar invents `column_definition` nodes named ENABLE and FORCE out of `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, which the analyzer faithfully published as columns. The repair panel has no bucket for 'the vanished symbol was a grammar-induced phantom' or 'the gained node was a clause the old grammar dropped', which is a real gap in F11's vocabulary and the reason a raw INADMISSIBLE is not the last word.

internal_silent._description: Grammar-internal containers, keywords and expression nodes that correctly emit nothing: they carry no declaration and no relationship semantics in the analyzer's contract. The keyword_* family is deliberately silent — a keyword is never a table and never a function, which is the SQL-D3 ruling below and the reason the analyzer's own SQL_KEYWORDS guard exists.

gap._description: Confirmed missing emissions and known grammar limits, numbered SQL-G*. Tracked work items, not gate failures. Each carries the measurement that established it. Two were added 2026-09-27 after a SECOND corpus was found on this machine and the lane had never been run against it; the six below were all written from app-migration files, which is why the plpgsql gap looked smaller than it is. SQL-G11..SQL-G14 added 2026-10-03 by the ontology workstream; G13 and G14 are shared-machinery findings filed rather than fixed. LANE VERIFICATION 2026-10-09 (firing + incoming + full-corpus census). THE 120-FILE FIRING SAMPLE IS NOT REPRESENTATIVE FOR THIS LANE, and that is the finding that reorders every gap below. `script/m14/firing-check.mjs` samples the first N files in directory-walk order; on `fixtures/repositories/duckdb` that order is `benchmark/clickbench/queries`, `benchmark/aoc24/queries`, `benchmark/imdb_plan_cost/queries` — read-only analytics SELECTs. MEASURED: only 5 of the first 120 sampled files contain any `CREATE/ALTER/DROP` at all (4.2%), 42 of 300 (14.0%), 108 of all 594 (18.2%). A type whose construct is DDL therefore CANNOT fire in the default sample however correct the analyzer is, and the baseline line `2 types fired … SILENT: extends implements imports exports contains references overrides instantiates` was read as eight defects where it is one sampling artefact plus three grammar absences. Re-running the SAME instrument widened (`NFILES=300 bun script/m14/firing-check.mjs SQL`) fires `contains:653`. THE DENOMINATOR INSTRUMENT is `bun validation/m14/fixtures/sql/lane-census.ts <corpus> 0 [--pools]`, which walks the WHOLE corpus (594 duckdb `.sql`; 1,526 pooled across 20 repos) through the production path and counts, per type, the edges, the files, the ANALYZER'S OWN construct sites read from the tree, and the resolution outcome using the incoming gate's own rule (`script/m14/incoming-rule.ts`), so the two instruments cannot disagree about what 'unresolved' means. DUCKDB, 594 files, 594 parsed: contains 1070 edges in 85 files, 1070 resolving to exactly one declaration, 0 ambiguous, 0 unresolved; references 1 edge in 1 file (1 ambiguous); imports 0 edges with 0 construct sites; overrides 0 edges with 0 replacement pairs; instantiates 0 edges with 24 custom-type cast sites; extends/implements/exports 0 edges with 0 grammar nodes. POOLED, 1,526 files, 1,526 parsed: contains 5400/433 files/5183 resolved/217 ambiguous/0 unresolved; imports 38 edges in 14 files against 38 precise sites (22 psql includes in 6 files + 16 CREATE EXTENSION in 9 files, a 1:1 match); references 2092/275 files/1687 resolved/333 ambiguous/72 unresolved against 486 FK positions in 98 files; instantiates 21/11 resolved/8 ambiguous/2 unresolved against 184 custom-type casts in 35 files. INCOMING GATE, the lane's second acceptance criterion, run as `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts sql sql 60`: BEFORE `FAIL — 110 ambiguous + 289 unresolved of 1709 edges`; AFTER this round `FAIL — 97 ambiguous + 281 unresolved of 1696 edges … 8 external claim(s) unverifiable (0 verified + 8 unverifiable external)`. The overrides identity fix is the whole of the ambiguous movement (14 -> 1 on this population) and the pg_catalog marker is the whole of the unresolved movement on the sample. INSTANTIATES SIZED 2026-10-09 and RULED NOT-UNDER-DELIVERING, so no analyzer change was made. `bun validation/m14/fixtures/sql/instantiates-sizing.ts <corpus> [--pools]` replays the analyzer's OWN funnel (`constructsAValue`, `referenceLeaf`) over a full independent tree walk and reports where each `cast` site stops. DUCKDB, 594 files: 1286 `cast` nodes, 24 carry a `custom_type` FIELD -> 5 stopped as a keyword/builtin target (D3), 0 with no readable target, 0 with no value side, 14 stopped because the VALUE SIDE HAS AN ERROR, 5 stopped as CONVERSIONS the D13 exclusion covers, and **0 CONSTRUCTIONS**. So the 0 edges against 24 sites is the ruling working, not a miss. The 14 damaged parses are all DuckDB inline type syntax the wired grammar cannot read (`CAST(x AS STRUCT(a FLOAT, b FLOAT))` x11, `0]::aoc2022_day19_vec4` x3) - see SQL-G17. POOLED, 1526 files: 4630 casts, 184 with a `custom_type` -> 7 builtin, 14 damaged, 127 conversions, **36 CONSTRUCTIONS**. The analyzer emits 21 `instantiates` edges over those 36 sites, and the decisive measurement is at (file, target) granularity, where the edge key lives: the 36 sites occupy **17 distinct (file, target) pairs and 0 of them lacks an edge**. 21 > 17 because the edge key is (type, source, target) and the source varies by statement; 36 > 21 because repeated sites in one file with one source collapse. Both directions are the intended graph semantics - one edge per dependency fact, not one per call site - so NOT ONE construction site is missed. The conversion bucket was audited rather than trusted: by value node type it is literal 94, parenthesized_expression 10, invocation 8, field 5, parameter 5, binary_expression 2, cast 2, object_reference 1; the 8 invocation-valued ones - the only bucket a real constructor could hide in, since `constructsAValue` accepts only a callee literally named `row` - are `now()::wh_timestamp` (7) and `xmlconcat2(state, next.xml)::"text/xml"` (1), both genuine conversions of a value that already existed. POPULATION CORRECTION 2026-10-11 — every `POOLED, 1,526 files` figure in this description is an UNDER-MEASUREMENT and must not be quoted as a whole-corpus number. `repositories/proxicall` is a SYMLINK and the census walk tested `readdirSync(...,{withFileTypes:true}).isDirectory()`, which is FALSE for a symlink, so 439 .sql files — 22.3% of the 1,965-file population — were dropped in silence. Same instrument, same corpus, only the walk fixed: admitted 1,526 -> 1,965, TOTAL edges 16,273 -> 31,051, imports 38 -> 53, overrides 7 -> 8, instantiates 21 (unchanged), references 2,092 -> 5,966, contains 5,400 -> 12,024, uses 6,740 -> 9,106, calls 1,975 -> 3,873. The corrected artifact is validation/m14/fixtures/sql/lane-census-pooled.json (the 1,526-file run is preserved, stamped, as lane-census-pooled.SUPERSEDED-1526-files.json). CROSS-TAB against the incoming gate over the same population: imports 53 = 53, overrides 8 = 8, instantiates 21 = 21 — the three contested types agree EXACTLY; every other type is within 0.9% and the total within 0.8%. WHERE THIS DESCRIPTION SAYS 'POOLED, 1,526 files', READ THE CORRECTED FIGURE OR THE WHOLE-CORPUS TABLE IN validation/m14/fixtures/sql/whole-corpus-typing.txt.

gaps.missing: A dollar-quoted body whose statements the grammar cannot parse (RAISE, GET DIAGNOSTICS, LOOP) yields no `create_function` node at all. The opaque whole-body token that would fix it is unreachable while a structured alternative competes for the start tag (see grammar_provenance.removed_after_measurement), and making it reachable would mean deleting the structured forms that keep a PARSEABLE body's inner statements visible. Measured residual: the statement is reported in errors[] and the declarations after it survive via the analyzer's sweep and resync, but the function symbol itself is not emitted.
gaps.evidence: fixtures/sql/probe/contract-battery.mts + validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld9-declaration-resync.sql (documents the residual rather than claiming it)

CLOSED 2026-10-09 by measurement, and the text below is kept only to record what was true before SQL-D11 landed. `imports` IS emitted, on two separately labelled mechanisms. Measured with the corpus census: over the 1,526-file pooled corpus the analyzer emits 38 `imports` edges in 14 files against exactly 38 precise construct sites counted independently from the tree — 22 `psql_meta_command` nodes whose text begins `\i`/`\ir` and names a target, in 6 files, plus 16 `create_extension` nodes in 9 files. A 1:1 edge-per-site match is the strongest form this claim can take: no site is missed and no edge is invented. In the 594-file duckdb corpus the type has 0 sites (0 `psql_meta_command` nodes, 0 `create_extension` nodes, 0 files matching a line-initial `\i`/`\ir`, 0 files matching `create extension`) and correctly emits 0 edges — which is what a RULED-inapplicable type looks like, and it is the reason this gap appeared open. OVERTURN CONDITION unchanged: a `\i`/`\ir` argument that is a psql variable or carries no filename suffix.

gaps.missing: The analyzer emits no `exports`. SQL has no export syntax, and every schema entity is by definition declared; populating the channel would fabricate. Left empty on purpose, not forgotten.

A policy's USING / WITH CHECK expressions and a GRANT's privilege list are not walked for the tables they name. A policy that reads another table through its predicate (`USING (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM other_table …))`) yields the policy symbol and its `ON` edge but not the predicate's tables, because the analyzer reads the statement's top-level object_references only.
gaps.evidence: measured while wiring processPolicy; the predicate subtree is reachable but is not yet descended into

gaps.missing: PL/pgSQL procedural scaffolding is absent from the wired grammar: IF/ELSIF/ELSE/END IF, LOOP, WHILE, FOR ... IN, BEGIN/EXCEPTION/END, assignment, RAISE, EXECUTE, PERFORM, ASSERT and EXIT/CONTINUE. A body is parseable only if every statement in it is ordinary SQL. This is the single largest measured gap in the lane: 56.7% of all CREATE declarations across the three corpora sit inside a dollar-quoted body, and on the PostgreSQL extension corpus function recall is 17.6% (2,095 of 11,883) with 55 of 387 files yielding zero symbols. A full candidate was written and built (17 rules, 16 keywords, reusing $._expression and $.statement rather than reimplementing plpgsql expressions) and measured: -36% ProxiCall error nodes, +9.4% named nodes, 0 product change on the first build because it regressed the block-declarations contract case. The regression's cause is diagnosed and the fix is one line plus one declared conflict.

DDL handed to the database as a string is now RECOVERED for the shape `EXECUTE [IMMEDIATE] '<sql>'` by the analyzer's text-based EXECUTE-literal pass (shipped 2026-09-27; +156 symbols and +234 relationships on the extension corpus). Two shapes remain out of reach and are named rather than quietly dropped. (a) `EXECUTE format('CREATE TABLE %I', x)`, where the literal does not immediately follow the EXECUTE keyword. (b) CONCATENATED FRAGMENTS — 94% of the extension corpus's EXECUTE literals are `EXECUTE 'CREATE SEQUENCE ' || quote_ident(x) || ...`, where the literal is three words and the declaration's NAME is computed at run time. The pass recovers the KIND; the name is unrecoverable in principle, and no extension of the technique changes that. Only 78 of those literals are standalone statements.

`CREATE TABLE archive (LIKE source INCLUDING ALL)` is parsed but not read. Measured corpus-wide: 9 occurrences in 4 files, `keyword_like` 574 nodes over the census corpus (the rest are `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA x LIKE 'pattern'`, which name no table). The clause is a structural COPY, not inheritance - the two tables evolve independently - so it is not an `extends` edge; and the nearest honest label for the dependency it does create is one this analyzer does not currently emit. No edge is published for it, deliberately, rather than published as a relationship whose type would be arguable.
gaps.evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/construct-probe.json (constructCounts.extends-like = 9, examples name the three proxicall archive tables) and validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld13-ontology-types.sql, whose forbidRelationships pins that `LIKE`'s target is NOT edged

gaps.missing: `ALTER TABLE log ADD KEY useragent_id (useragent_id)` is MySQL's index-adding syntax and the grammar reads it as a column named `KEY` of type `useragent_id`, which the analyzer publishes. Measured at 1 phantom symbol corpus-wide (cloogle.org/db/install.sql line 25). NOT guarded: the tree cannot distinguish it from `ALTER TABLE t ADD key my_type`, which is legal PostgreSQL, so a text guard on `KEY` would delete a real column to remove a phantom. Declared rather than fixed; `LIKE`/`INHERIT` are guarded because those two are reserved in every dialect this grammar serves.
gaps.evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/construct-probe.json and the phantom probe run over the 1,460-file census (1 occurrence, named file and line)

gaps.missing: `contains` exists and is the lane's best-resolved type, but it only ever connects a TABLE to its members. A schema contains no table and a file contains no schema or table, so the containment tree has no root and a schema-qualified schema's members hang off the table instead of off the schema. Measured with the corpus census: over the 594-file duckdb corpus 1070 `contains` edges in 85 files carry `metadata.memberKind` `property` 1069 and `constant` 1 and NOTHING else; over the 1,526-file pooled corpus 5400 edges carry `property` 4886 and `constant` 514. Zero edges in either corpus has a namespace (schema) or module (file) as its member, although 33 `create_schema` declarations exist in the pooled corpus and every table, view, index, function and sequence is declared in some file. Reproduced minimally and deterministically: `bun validation/m14/fixtures/sql/contains-shape-probe.ts` on a four-statement schema (`CREATE SCHEMA app; CREATE TABLE app.users (...); CREATE INDEX ...; CREATE VIEW app.active ...`) reports `namespace:app` and `class:users`/`class:active` among the symbols and exactly THREE containment edges, all `class -> property|constant`; the pairs app->users, app->active and file->app are absent. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED rather than ruled: the edge is a fact the grammar states, the analyzer already builds both endpoint symbols, and the reason it does not exist is that `processTable` and its siblings pass `parent: null` to `createSymbol`, with the schema not yet known when the declaration is walked (declaration order in a migration is not the order the passes visit), so the fix is a post-pass in the shape of `adoptLateDeclaredIndexOwners` and `retargetContainmentEdges`. Sized, not estimated: 33 `create_schema` sites pooled, and every schema-qualified declaration whose schema prefix names a schema the same file declares is a candidate.
gaps.evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/lane-census-pooled.json and lane-census-duckdb.json (contains by memberKind: property/constant only) and validation/m14/fixtures/sql/contains-shape-probe.ts (committed minimal reproduction)

gaps.missing: The analyzer's external classification reaches the arbiter for ONE of its four kinds. It writes the KIND into `metadata.external` as a string (`external: "postgresCatalog"`), and `script/m14/incoming-rule.ts` accepts an external claim only when a key in `EXTERNAL_KEYS` is `=== true`, so before this round the classification was inert and an edge the analyzer had correctly labelled landed in the gate's plain `unresolved` column. Measured over the 1,526-file pooled census: 191 not-resolved edges carried `metadata.external`, of which 6 were already valued `true` (the CREATE EXTENSION imports arm) and 185 were kind strings the arbiter could not read — postgresCatalog 125, informationSchema 52, platform 8. `postgresCatalog` is now also marked `isExternal: true` because it is the one arm where the claim is a documented fact about the LANGUAGE rather than a guess about a spelling: PostgreSQL's schema chapter says `pg_catalog` "is implicitly searched before searching the path's schemas", so an unqualified `pg_class` denotes the system catalog and cannot denote a project table. Measured effect: 125 edges move out of `unresolved` (the gate sample shows uses 213 -> 205 and calls 48; the pooled census shows uses 888 -> 769 and calls 973 -> 967) with 0 REFUTED, and the marker cannot raise `resolved`. DELIBERATELY NOT MARKED, and left as a measured gap: `informationSchema` 52 (`tables` 20, `columns` 13, `table_constraints` 9, `views` 6, `key_column_usage` 2, `constraint_column_usage` 1, `referential_constraints` 1) because its bare-name arm is a list of ordinary words and a project table with one of those names is reachable by search-path order; and `platform` 8 (`algorithm_sign` 4, `url_decode` 3, `encrypt_pass` 1) because it fires on helper FUNCTION names whose owning schema is not in the target string. Neither can be verified or refuted by the population (0 verified / 0 refuted of 60), so marking them would excuse a gap with a claim nothing can check. RECONCILIATION 2026-10-09 — two coverage numbers describe two DIFFERENT SETS, and the record must carry both definitions because a verifier re-running the census sees only the second. (A) `markedExternalReadable = 125`: every edge carrying `isExternal: true` (all of them `postgresCatalog`), counted by KEY PRESENCE over all 16,273 pooled edges regardless of outcome. All 125 now classify as `externalUnverified`, i.e. all 125 LEFT `unresolved` — which is the number this lane reported as the marker's effect (uses 888 -> 769 = 119, calls 973 -> 967 = 6). (B) `notResolvedStillCarryingExternalValue = 66`: edges whose outcome is STILL `unresolved`/`ambDeclOnly`/`ambBoth` AND which still carry a `metadata.external` value — 6 boolean + 60 strings, i.e. the residual gap that still wears an unreadable external label. THE TWO SETS ARE DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the whole explanation: the arbiter's rule reads a claim only when the target names no declaration, and a claim it can read sends the edge to `externalUnverified` — the third bucket the rule defines as "visible, counted, and deliberately not merged into either of the other two". `externalUnverified` is therefore NOT `unresolved`, so a marked edge cannot appear in (B) however it is counted. The instrument prints (B), not (A). THE 191 SEEN EARLIER IS THE PRE-MARKER STATE OF (B), not a third population: before the marker the same section printed 191 = 6 boolean + 185 strings (postgresCatalog 125 + informationSchema 52 + platform 8); after it, 66 = 6 boolean + 60 strings (informationSchema 52 + platform 8). 185 - 60 = 125, which is exactly (A). Both rows are the same instrument on the same 1,526-file population; only the analyzer changed between them. Quoting 191 and 125 in one paragraph without labelling the state change is what made the record look inconsistent, and that was an error of exposition in this lane's report, not of measurement. NOT UNDER-DELIVERY, and this is measured rather than argued: `bun validation/m14/fixtures/sql/external-marker-audit.ts $HOME/fixtures/repositories --pools` counts by key presence, value type and outcome independently of any difference of runs, and reports `metadata.external === "postgresCatalog"` on 125 edges and `isExternal === true` on 125 edges — the SAME 125 — so the marker fires on the entire classified population and no `pg_catalog` edge is left behind. It also reports `notResolved AND isExternal === true = 0`: no marked edge is still counted as a gap. FALSIFIER, re-confirmed on this population: `externalRefuted = 0` of 16,273 edges.
gaps.evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/lane-census-pooled.json (EXTERNAL-VISIBILITY SPLIT section, including the classified target names) and validation/m14/fixtures/sql/lane-gate-AFTER-external.txt; validation/m14/fixtures/sql/external-marker-audit.ts and external-marker-audit-pooled.txt (key-presence / value-type / outcome audit, the reconciliation instrument)

gaps.missing: A composite-typed cast whose VALUE SIDE the wired grammar cannot parse, so the analyzer refuses to publish a construction it cannot vouch for. Measured with the instantiates sizing funnel (`bun validation/m14/fixtures/sql/instantiates-sizing.ts`): 14 such sites in the 594-file duckdb corpus and 14 in the 1,526-file pooled corpus, in exactly two shapes. (a) DuckDB's inline composite type - `CAST((NULL) AS STRUCT(x FLOAT, y FLOAT))`, `CAST(("Q"."point") AS STRUCT(here INTEGER, there INTEGER, length INTEGER))` - 11 of the 14, where the grammar reads the literal word `STRUCT` as the `custom_type` name and cannot parse the parenthesised field list, so the value side carries an ERROR node. (b) the bracketed array literal - `0]::aoc2022_day19_vec4` - 3 of the 14, where `[a+b, ...]::vec4` parses as `ERROR :: type`. The analyzer already names both shapes in `processInstantiations`' own comment and skips them deliberately: a damaged parse is not a construction the analyzer can vouch for, and publishing one would assert a `ROW(...)` construction where the tree only shows an ERROR. This is a GRAMMAR limit in the same family as SQL-G3 (vendor dialects) and is filed separately because it has a named instrument and a count rather than a bare error-node tally. NOT fixed: the fix is a grammar rule for DuckDB's inline `STRUCT(...)` type and for bracketed array literals, which is a grammar change, not an analyzer one. OVERTURN CONDITION: a `cast` whose value side carries no ERROR and whose target is a declared type, in one of these two shapes.
gaps.evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/instantiates-sizing-pooled.txt (DAMAGED-PARSE SITES section, with the site texts) and validation/m14/fixtures/sql/instantiates-sizing.ts

gaps.missing: `src/ast/pool-worker.ts`'s `NOISE_TARGETS` list contains `root`, so `keepSymbol` deletes a real project symbol with that name on the way to the index. Measured over the 1,460-file census by `validation/m14/fixtures/sql/keep-symbol-census.mts`: 14,851 symbols emitted, 2 dropped (0.013%), both `function:root` - `postgrest/test/io/fixtures/schema.sql` declares `create or replace function root() returns json`. This is the same defect class that file's own comment documents for `type`, `parent` and `firstChild`, and `root` is still on the list. Shared machinery: filed, not edited. An earlier draft of this record said 3 drops from an ad-hoc probe that was not committed; the committed instrument says 2 and the committed number is the one that stands.
gaps.evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/keep-symbol-census.json (analyzer `analyze` plus the exported pool-worker `keepSymbol`, over the same 1,460 admitted files)

gaps.missing: `script/m14/differential.ts` has no SQL oracle, so every relationship type this lane emits is a DERIVATION finding: stored and compared against nothing. Measured: 68 per-language `derive*Edges` functions exist and none is SQL's; a scoped run against ProxiCall (437 SQL files, 60 sampled) exits with `derived ZERO truth edges`. The lane's own 84-fact hand audit is the only correctness instrument it has, and an audit of 84 facts over 5 fixtures cannot stand in for a differential over a corpus. Shared machinery: filed, not edited.

design_decision.description: SQL schema contract (M60 SQL wave, ruled 2026-09-26/27). A SQL file is a SCHEMA, not a program: the declarations are the product, the relationships are containment plus data dependencies, and there is no import graph. ONTOLOGY WORKSTREAM (2026-10-03): SQL-D11..SQL-D18 carry the ten-type verdicts. Three types were newly EMITTED against a corpus measurement (imports, overrides, instantiates), one previous ruling was FALSIFIED by that measurement (SQL-D11), four are RULED with a named instrument and a probe, and the remainder record what the census found about the edges that were already emitted. ONTOLOGY ROUND 2 (2026-10-03, same lane): SQL-D19 records a fabricated `uses` edge the lane's own oracle caught and SQL-D20 records that all seven emitted types are DERIVATION findings because the shared differential has no SQL oracle. `CREATE EXTENSION` was added to `imports` as a second, separately labelled mechanism (27 of the 49 `imports` edges), taking that type from the RULED column to EMITTED. LANE VERIFICATION ROUND (2026-10-09): SQL-D21 records that a routine's override identity is its ARGUMENT TYPES, not its name, and that both fixtures asserting the opposite were wrong rather than the analyzer; SQL-D22 records which of the four external classifications the arbiter can read and why only one of them is marked; SQL-D23 records the still-open state of the containment tree (SQL-G15). The three types this round was asked to work were measured rather than assumed, and the answer for two of them is that they were never silent: `contains` fires 1070 edges over the 594-file duckdb corpus with 0 unresolved and 5400 over the 1,526-file pooled corpus, and `imports` fires 38 edges against exactly 38 independently counted construct sites. The 'silent' reading came from `script/m14/firing-check.mjs`'s default sample, which for this corpus is 95.8% DDL-free query text — see gap._description for the composition measurement. SQL-D24 records the `instantiates` sizing that RULED the type correct and changed no code: 0 constructions among duckdb's 24 custom-type cast sites, and on the pooled corpus every distinct construction site already produces an edge.

decisions.question: Is a column's declared TYPE a dependency edge? A user-defined type is an `object_reference` in this grammar, exactly like a `REFERENCES` target.
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO. A foreign key is an `object_reference` that FOLLOWS `keyword_references`; the discriminator is position in the grammar, not a guess. The previous rule (any object_reference child) minted `references t -> my_type` plus the 'Foreign Key Constraints' pattern for every custom-typed column — measured on the corpus as one phantom FK per custom-typed column.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld1-column-types.sql (forbidRelationships) and mutant sql/custom-column-type-is-a-foreign-key

decisions.question: Which object_reference is a trigger's action routine?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the LAST top-level one, with the table taken from the reference after `keyword_on`. Reading the first three anywhere in the subtree resolved the action to `old` whenever the trigger has a `WHEN (old.a <> new.a)` clause, because old/new are object_references in this grammar.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld2-trigger-when.sql and mutant sql/trigger-action-read-from-the-when-clause

decisions.question: Can a SQL reserved word be a relationship target or a call target?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO, never. A keyword is not a table and not a function. The guard is on the emitted edge AND at the call site, so an ERROR-recovery artefact cannot reach the graph from any path. Measured 49 keyword-target edges over 441 corpus files before the guard (`calls global->USING`, `uses global->WITH`, `calls …->FILTER`) and 0 after. Symmetrically, a call to a function SQL itself provides is a language feature, not a dependency the store could ever resolve — the builtin set covers aggregate, window, numeric, string, date/time, conditional, JSON, array and system functions.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld6-keyword-and-builtin.sql (whose last row is the CONTROL that stops a fix from simply dropping every call) and mutant sql/keyword-becomes-a-relationship-target

decisions.question: How far does a CTE name shadow?
decisions.resolution: RULED: only its own UNQUALIFIED reference. Matching on the bare leaf suppressed a real table too — `WITH a AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM a JOIN s.a ON true` emitted no relationship at all. A qualified reference is never a CTE.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld5-quoted-and-cte.sql and mutant sql/cte-shadows-a-qualified-reference

decisions.question: Should an edge target be the qualified reference (`app.orders`) or the bare leaf (`orders`)?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the BARE LEAF, with the qualified text preserved in the relationship metadata. Measured on 441 files / 6,917 edges against the store's own three resolution strategies (S1 exact qualified_name, S2 bare name when globally unique, S3 dotted tail): bare resolves 6,180 (0.8935) and qualified 2,132 (0.3082), because most references in a real schema are written unqualified. `decisiveQualifiedRefs: 0` — no reference in the corpus is both written qualified and ambiguously bare, so qualifying buys nothing measurable.
decisions.pinned_by: fixtures/sql/probe/edge-resolvability.mts (screening instrument, not a gate)

decisions.question: How does the analyzer cope with a parse that collapses a whole file into one ERROR?
decisions.resolution: RULED: two layers, both measured. (1) A full-tree declaration sweep, which finds declarations that error recovery nested inside an unrelated statement — 1,644 of 2,336 corpus declarations against 1,557 for a root-children walk. (2) A statement-level resync that re-parses top-level statement slices with their ranges translated back to file coordinates, and is STRICTLY ADDITIVE: the main pass's declarations are keyed by absolute start index, so a re-parsed slice can only contribute what was missing. The resync fires on cumulative multi-error files and on NO synthetic fixture — the grammar patch fixed every cascade a minimal fixture is built from — so it is pinned by a CORPUS gate (script/m60/verify-sql-resync.ts) rather than a mutant, and the mutant suite records that a fixture mutant for it could not be shown to fail. A gate that cannot fail is decoration.
decisions.pinned_by: script/m60/verify-sql-resync.ts (C1 reachability, C2 every firing recovers, C3 recovered ranges are file-absolute 1-based) and validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld9-declaration-resync.sql

decisions.question: Are symbol range columns 0- or 1-based?
decisions.resolution: RULED: 1-BASED, matching the engine's own ParseError range (engine.ts parseFile) and the seven sibling analyzers that build a range. The SQL helper was the only 0-based range in the tree, so all four column fields of every SQL symbol were off by one corpus-wide. The resync's slice translation carries the same base, which is why its recovered ranges are checked for absoluteness rather than assumed.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld8-range-and-ids.sql (expectSymbolRanges) and mutant sql/range-columns-zero-based

decisions.question: What is a top-level SQL symbol's identity when two entities share a bare name?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the name, disambiguated on collision. `id` was `parentId ?? name`, so `CREATE TABLE a.t` and `CREATE TABLE b.t` both got id `t` — duplicate ids drop nodes from id-keyed graph consumers and conflate two distinct declarations (the family RSD3 class). Relationship endpoints stay NAMES, which is what the store's resolution strategies key on.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld8-range-and-ids.sql (expectUniqueIds) and mutant sql/same-name-declarations-share-an-id

decisions.question: Is a quoted identifier's name `"MyTable"` or `MyTable`?
decisions.resolution: RULED: `MyTable`. The delimiter is SQL syntax, not part of the name. The shipped analyzer kept the quotes for `"…"`, kept the backticks for `` `…` ``, and lost the column entirely for `"Id"` — the grammar puts a quoted name in a `literal`, never an `identifier` — so the three quoting styles behaved three different ways and one of them dropped the symbol.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld5-quoted-and-cte.sql

decisions.question: What does the analyzer report for a file it cannot parse?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the ERROR and MISSING nodes, on the analyzer's own channel, with severity `warning` (the value the indexer keys hasSyntaxErrors off). It previously returned `errors: []` unconditionally, so a file it could not parse at all read as a clean 0/0/0 — and the fixture lane, the mutation harness and the m12 differential all call `analyze` directly, so the analyzer's channel is the one they read.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld7-error-honesty.sql and mutant sql/parse-errors-never-reported

decisions.question: ONTOGY / `imports` — this lane previously ruled that "SQL has no import statement", on the grounds that the previous implementation scanned for `#import`/`@import` text the grammar can never produce. Does the LANGUAGE have an import?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the EARLIER RULING IS FALSIFIED and `imports` is now EMITTED. The earlier reasoning was sound about the MECHANISM and wrong about the LANGUAGE, which is exactly the failure a ruling has to be falsifiable to catch. Measured over the 1,460-file census with instrument B (parse-tree semantic count): 143 `psql_meta_command` nodes, of which 22 are `\i`/`\ir` naming another file with a literal filename, across 6 files; 121 are `\echo`(108)/`\set`(8)/`\gexec`/`\if`/`\endif`/`\gset`/`\pset`, none of which names a file; includes with a psql VARIABLE target: 0; includes with no recognisable filename suffix: 0. `\i` and `\ir` are imports in the ordinary sense: a file dependency resolved by the psql client before any SQL runs. postgrest/test/io/fixtures/load.sql includes six sibling scripts this way. OVERTURN CONDITION for the guards: a corpus file whose `\i`/`\ir` argument is a psql variable or carries no .sql/.psql/.dump suffix would move that event into `ambiguity.includeNonLiteral` and the analyzer would still emit nothing for it — deliberately, since a target invented from a variable name is a fabricated edge. SECOND MECHANISM, added after the extension case was measured rather than argued. `CREATE EXTENSION name` loads a separately DISTRIBUTED unit and the file cannot mean anything without it. `processNamedContainer` recorded the declaration as a `module` symbol and emitted no edge, so over the 1,460-file census 27 declarations in 8 files were 27 symbols with zero dependencies - a real cross-unit dependency invisible in the graph, in the one construct where SQL genuinely has one. It is now published as `imports` with `metadata.extensionInstall: true`, `external: true`, `fileDependency: false`, `scope: "database"`, and as an `imports[]` row with `importType: "sql_extension"`. The flags are load-bearing rather than documentation: a psql include names a FILE IN THIS REPOSITORY and is resolvable in principle, while an extension names a distribution that can never bind to anything this repository contains, and a consumer that cannot tell them apart will try to resolve `global->hstore` as a path. This is also the strongest candidate against the `exports` ruling (SQL-D16) and it is answered with a measurement: 27 occurrences, and the direction the construct points is inbound. Total `imports` over the census is 49 (22 + 27), and the type resolves at 55.10% because the 27 extension targets cannot resolve by construction.

decisions.question: ONTOGY / `overrides` — SQL has no method table, so is there any replacement event at all?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES, and it is `CREATE OR REPLACE`. Measured with instrument B over the 1,460-file census: 666 declarations carry `OR REPLACE`; 15 replace a declaration of the SAME KIND in the SAME FILE and are therefore visible to a per-file analyzer, which is what the analyzer now emits; 20 same-kind re-declarations carry NO `OR REPLACE` and PostgreSQL rejects those outright, so calling them overrides would assert a replacement the language does not perform. Declared limit: the other 651 replace a declaration made in ANOTHER file (a migration chain re-declaring the previous migration's function), which a per-file analyzer cannot see and does not claim. OVERTURN CONDITION: a corpus file with two `OR REPLACE` declarations of one name and no intervening `DROP` would add an edge; a same-kind duplicate WITHOUT `OR REPLACE` deliberately will not.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld13-ontology-types.sql (expectRelationshipCount overrides=2, forbidRelationships on d13_only_once and d13_twin) and mutants sql/any-redeclaration-becomes-an-override

decisions.question: ONTOGY / `instantiates` — SQL has no `new`, so is there any construction of an instance of a declared type?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES, and it is a composite-type cast. PostgreSQL implements `ROW(1,2)::my_composite` as a call to that type's constructor. Measured with instrument B over the 1,460-file census: 4,406 `cast` nodes, of which only those carrying a `custom_type` FIELD name a user type (a builtin target such as `::integer` is a bare anonymous token, so no hand-written builtin-type list is needed); 20 are a constructor-shaped value against a type the corpus declares, 4 are a conversion against a declared type, and 67 target a name no file declares (`::row`, `::struct`, `::geometry` — DuckDB inline type specifications and extension types). The analyzer emits `instantiates` only for the construction-shaped case. OVERTURN CONDITION: a corpus cast whose `custom_type` names a declared type and whose value side is a `ROW(...)` invocation or a `list`/`array` node would add an edge; a conversion must not.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld13-ontology-types.sql (expectRelationshipCount instantiates=1, forbidRelationships on d13_never_built and integer) and mutant sql/any-cast-becomes-an-instantiation

decisions.question: ONTOGY / `extends` — is table inheritance (`CREATE TABLE c (...) INHERITS (p)`, `ALTER TABLE c INHERIT p`) readable from this grammar?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NOT READABLE, and the ruling is a statement about the wired grammar rather than about SQL. Instrument B over the 1,460-file census: 0 occurrences of an `INHERITS`/`INHERIT` token inside a `create_table` or `alter_table` node. The stronger evidence is a capability probe rather than a corpus count: parsing `CREATE TABLE child (id int) INHERITS (parent);` with the wired wasm yields `create_table` terminated at the column list followed by `ERROR(identifier)` — the grammar has no rule for the clause, so `INHERITS` cannot appear in the tree in any corpus. SQL DOES have this construct, so a grammar that could express it would make `extends` derivable; until one does, emitting the edge would mean inventing it. OVERTURN CONDITION: a `keyword_inherits`/`inherits_clause` node inside `create_table`, or a corpus file where the token survives parse in that position. The adjacent `LIKE` clause IS parsed (`keyword_like`, 574 nodes corpus-wide, 9 of them inside a `create_table`) and is a structural COPY rather than inheritance — the two tables evolve independently — so it is deliberately not an `extends` edge; see SQL-D15.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld13-ontology-types.sql for the LIKE clause's non-extends classification (forbidRelationships contains d13_archive->d13_holder), and validation/m14/fixtures/sql/construct-probe.json for the INHERITS=0 measurement

decisions.question: The wired grammar cannot represent `CREATE TABLE c (LIKE p INCLUDING ALL)`: it parses the pair as `column_definition name:(identifier "LIKE") custom_type:(object_reference "p")`. Is that a column, and does the LIKE clause's target belong in the graph?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NOT a column, and the LIKE target is not edged here. Measured corpus-wide with instrument B: 6 `column_definition` nodes named `LIKE` in 2 files, each of which the analyzer published as a column whose fabricated `sqlType` is the source table; the analyzer now suppresses them (`ambiguity.reservedNameSymbolsSuppressed`) and the same shape makes `ALTER TABLE c INHERIT p` a column named `INHERIT`. The guard keys on the name AND on the node being an UNQUOTED `identifier`, because `LIKE` and `INHERIT` are reserved in every dialect this grammar serves while a quoted `"like"` column arrives as a `literal` and is legal. NOT fixed: `ALTER TABLE log ADD KEY k (c)` parses identically to `ALTER TABLE t ADD key my_type`, which is legal PostgreSQL, so a text guard would trade one wrong symbol for a missing one; measured at 1 phantom corpus-wide and declared rather than hidden. The LIKE target itself is NOT published as an edge: the clause is a structural copy, the nearest ontology label is a dependency the analyzer does not currently read, and the 9 occurrences do not justify asserting one here — recorded as SQL-G11 rather than silently dropped.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld13-ontology-types.sql (forbidSymbols LIKE, expectSymbolCount LIKE=0 and the quoted like=1, forbidRelationships contains d13_archive->LIKE) and mutant sql/reserved-word-becomes-a-column

decisions.question: ONTOGY / `exports` and `implements` — is either derivable from SQL at all?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NEITHER, on two independent grounds each. `exports` would need a declaration naming the symbols this unit publishes to other units; SQL's visibility scope is the DATABASE, not the file, and nothing in a SQL file enumerates it. Instrument A: the wired grammar produces 465 distinct node types over the 1,460-file census and NONE is an export/module/provide statement — the full inventory is in validation/m14/fixtures/sql/construct-probe.json so the ruling is checkable without re-running anything. Instrument B: 0 occurrences of an `EXPORT`, `MODULE` or `PROVIDE` token, 0 export-shaped nodes, 0 `grant_statement` in any file that would carry a published surface. psql's file graph is real and its only edge is INBOUND (`\i`), which is why `imports` is emitted and `exports` is not. `implements` would need a supertype clause; SQL has no interface type and no clause in which a declaration names a supertype it satisfies. Instrument A: no supertype/interface/extends-clause node type among the 465. Instrument B: 0 `IMPLEMENTS` tokens, 0 implements-shaped nodes. `CREATE DOMAIN d AS t CHECK (...)` is a constraint-carrying alias and not interface satisfaction. OVERTURN CONDITION for either: any node type among the 465 inventory that expresses a published surface or a supertype clause, or any corpus token in the positions probed.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/construct-probe.json (grammarVocabulary, 465 types; constructCounts for implements-keyword/implements-node/exports-keyword/exports-node, all 0)

decisions.question: Are `declarationKeys` / `createSymbol`'s dedup identities safe when three passes produce nodes from RE-PARSED SLICES?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO without an explicit file-coordinate key, and that is now fixed. `node.startIndex` is relative to the PARSE that produced the node, and the statement resync pass and the EXECUTE-literal pass both parse a slice, so a slice-local key collides with whatever the main pass consumed at the same offset. Measured both ways over the 1,460-file census: 161 intra-file duplicate symbols (identical kind, name and range emitted twice) across 10 files before, 0 after; and the instant the dedup guard became load-bearing while the key was still slice-local, sqld11 lost `quoted_name`. `state.slice.byteOffset` maps a slice node back to its true position - the raw literal is handed to the parser with its `''` escapes intact precisely so it stays a contiguous substring of the file - so the file coordinate is both correct and unique. Separately, `processStatement` was calling `markDeclaration` and IGNORING the answer, so the sweep dispatched every top-level declaration a second time; no edge doubled (the maps deduplicate) but the work did and so did the counters: one `ROW(1,2)::t` reported `instantiationsEmitted: 2`.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld11-execute-literal.sql (the quoted_name row) and mutants sql/declaration-key-ignores-the-slice-offset, sql/declaration-dispatched-twice

decisions.question: Can the honesty contract's §4 requirement - that the heuristic/deterministic edge ratio be a COUNTABLE number - be answered for this lane?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NOT BEFORE THIS ROUND, and now it can. The census recorded `evidenceClass` ABSENT on 22,022 of 22,022 edges, which reads as 'no heuristics' and means 'nothing recorded'; an absent field is not the same claim as a uniformly `structural` one, and only one of them was true. Every edge now carries a tier derived from how it was actually derived: `structural` for a fact in a grammar-mandated position (every `contains`, every `imports`, every `overrides`, every `instantiates`, every `references` - the FK target sits after `keyword_references`, the trigger's and policy's table after `keyword_on`), `usage_contextual` for a name in a bare slot (a `uses` from a `from`/`relation` clause, an UNQUALIFIED `calls` callee) and `reference_qualified` for a name read through a QUALIFIED reference. `confidence` stays 1 throughout, and that is now a claim rather than an omission: no edge is a guess about a NAME, and where the analyzer genuinely cannot tell it emits nothing and counts the suppression in `ambiguity` instead.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld13-ontology-types.sql (meta.evidenceClass on an imports, an overrides and an instantiates row) and mutant sql/evidence-class-dropped

decisions.question: ONTOGY / `uses` — a CTE name is a local binding, not a table. Does every path that can read an unqualified reference see the CTE scope?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO, and it did not. `ParseState.localCtes` is documented as holding the scope of the statement and only the statement, and the main walk honours that because `processRoot` populates it before dispatching. The declaration sweep is a SEPARATE walk with no such step, and it dispatches nested `statement` nodes on purpose (that is what makes a plpgsql body contribute edges at all). It therefore reached a CTE body - itself a `statement` - with BOTH the per-node set built by `processQueryDependencies` and the file-level set empty, and `addTableEdge`'s guard `localCtes.has(leaf) || state.localCtes.has(leaf)` let the edge through. Measured by the lane's own 84-fact hand audit, which had been reporting exactly this and only this since the artifact was written: `FP rel:Queries.sql:uses:global:recent_users`, precision 0.988, `earliestFailingLayer=relationships`. The outer `FROM named_users` was suppressed correctly by the same guard, so the file published exactly the one edge it should not have. FIXED by giving the sweep the CTE scope of the nearest ANCESTOR `statement` and restoring it afterwards, because sibling statements carry their own WITH lists. The differential is now precision 1.000, recall 1.000, 0 FP, 0 FN, `earliestFailingLayer=none`, and the artifact is regenerated against the analyzer this commit ships, which also retires the recorded claim that the current precision was not established by any artifact. OVERTURN CONDITION: a naked unqualified reference inside a CTE body that names a table the same file also declares and that is not a CTE of any enclosing statement.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld5-quoted-and-cte.sql (forbidRelationships on d5_first, expectRelationships on the qualified d5_real so a fix cannot pass by over-suppressing) and mutant sql/declaration-sweep-drops-the-cte-scope

decisions.question: DERIVATION debt: how many relationship types does this lane emit that no differential ever audits?
decisions.resolution: RULED: ALL SEVEN. `script/m14/differential.ts` carries 68 per-language `derive*Edges` oracle functions (`deriveJavaEdges`, `deriveGoUses`, `deriveRustDeclaredTypeRefs`, `deriveBashEdges`, …) and NONE for SQL, so `calls`, `uses`, `contains`, `imports`, `references`, `overrides` and `instantiates` are all stored and compared against nothing. Run against the SQL lane the harness says so out loud rather than reporting a clean 0/0: `Error: differential: ProxiCall:sql parsed 60 file(s) and derived ZERO truth edges - the parser or the oracle is dead, not clean (a 0/0 row is a fabricated pass)`. This is the ontology gate's own blind spot one level up - a differential cannot see a type missing from BOTH sides - and it is why the census and the construct probe are the lane's primary instruments. The oracle belongs to shared machinery; the lane's contribution is the specification in its report, not an edit. What the lane CAN audit on its own, it does: the m12 differential against 84 hand-audited facts, which is independent of the analyzer and caught SQL-D19.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/ontology-census.json (7 emitted types) and the gate refusal quoted above; script/m60/sql-ontology-ruled.ts for the arbiter table

decisions.question: ONTOGY / `overrides` — is a re-declaration of a NAME a replacement, or is a routine identified by something more than its name?
decisions.resolution: RULED: A ROUTINE IS IDENTIFIED BY ITS INPUT ARGUMENT TYPES, so a `CREATE OR REPLACE` whose argument list differs is an OVERLOAD and replaces NOTHING. PostgreSQL's CREATE FUNCTION reference, quoted rather than paraphrased: "It is not possible to change the name or argument types of a function this way (if you tried, you would actually be creating a new, distinct function)", and "Two functions are considered the same if they have the same names and INPUT argument types, ignoring any OUT parameters" — which is also why OUT parameters are excluded from this key. The analyzer keyed `state.redeclared` on `kind:name`, so `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION f(a integer)` followed by `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION f(a integer, b integer)` published an `overrides` edge asserting a replacement the language does not perform. MEASURED on the 60-file incoming-gate population: `overrides` emitted 14 edges of which 0 resolved — ALL 14 were ambiguous — and the number of declarations each target matched WAS the file's overload count (`overloaded` 2, `overloaded_default` 4, `overloaded_html_form` 3, `overloaded_unnamed_param` 5). The fix keys a routine on `kind:name(argtype,…)`; the second round of that fix handles UNNAMED parameters, which `functionArgument` returns null for and which had collapsed to the empty string — the remaining four ambiguous names were all unnamed-parameter overloads (`overloaded_unnamed_param` 5, `overloaded_unnamed_json_jsonb_param` 3, `color` 2, `isodate` 2). After both rounds: the gate population reports 1 `overrides` edge and 1 ambiguous (a `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` whose bare name another file also declares — a property of the bare-leaf target convention, SQL-D5, not of this mechanism), and the leaked count is reported rather than silent as `ambiguity.overloadNotReplacementSkipped`. VIEWS keep the name-only key: PostgreSQL has no view overloading, so two `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v` really are one object replacing itself. BOTH FIXTURES WERE WRONG AND WERE CORRECTED, which is the part worth recording: sqld13 and sqld14 each asserted `f(a integer)` -> `f(a integer, b integer)` as an override, and sqld14's own comment recorded renaming the target to dodge `relationshipsByKey`'s (type, source, target) collapse — a workaround for the symptom of the same name-keyed identity. Each fixture now pins BOTH sides: a same-signature pair that must emit, and an overload pair that must not (`d13_overloaded`, `d14_overloaded` in forbidRelationships).
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/sql/sqld13-ontology-types.{sql,expectation.json} and sqld14-pass2-adversarial.{sql,expectation.json} (both directions); `npx tsx script/m14/run-fixtures.ts --lang sql` 17/17; `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts sql sql 60` overrides 14 edges/14 ambiguous -> 1 edge/1 ambiguous

decisions.question: INCOMING CONTRACT — the analyzer classifies a target as external and writes the KIND as a string; the arbiter reads only a boolean. Which classifications may be marked, and which must stay unresolved?
decisions.resolution: RULED: `postgresCatalog` IS MARKED, the other three are NOT. The classification machinery is unchanged and still writes the descriptive `metadata.external: <kind>`; a boolean `isExternal: true` is added ONLY where the claim is a documented fact about the language rather than a guess about a spelling. For `pg_*` it is: PostgreSQL's schema chapter states `pg_catalog` "is always effectively part of the search path … implicitly searched BEFORE searching the path's schemas", so an unqualified `pg_class` denotes the system catalog and cannot denote a project table. MEASURED over the 1,526-file pooled census: of 191 not-resolved edges carrying `metadata.external`, 125 are `postgresCatalog`, and marking them moves 125 out of `unresolved` (uses 888 -> 769, calls 973 -> 967) with **0 refuted** — the marker is read only where the target names no declaration, so it can never raise `resolved`. NOT MARKED, with the names and counts recorded in SQL-G16: `informationSchema` 52, because its bare-name arm is a list of ordinary words (`tables` 20, `columns` 13, `views` 6) that a project table could legitimately carry and reach by search-path order; and `platform` 8, because it fires on helper function names (`algorithm_sign` 4, `url_decode` 3, `encrypt_pass` 1) whose owning schema is not in the target string. decisions.question: Is `contains` actually silent, and if not, what is missing from it?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NOT SILENT, and the missing part is the ROOT of the tree. `contains` fires 1070 edges over the 594-file duckdb corpus (85 files, 1070 resolving to exactly one declaration, 0 ambiguous, 0 unresolved) and 5400 over the 1,526-file pooled corpus (433 files, 5183 resolved, 217 ambiguous, 0 unresolved). What it does NOT do is connect a schema to its tables or a file to its schema: every `metadata.memberKind` in both corpora is `property` or `constant`, so the only owner a containment edge has ever had is a table. The 'silent' reading this round started from was produced by `script/m14/firing-check.mjs`'s default 120-file sample, which for duckdb is directory-walk order over `benchmark/*/queries` and contains DDL in 5 files of 120; widening the SAME instrument to 300 files fires `contains:653`. The residual is an OPEN, SIZED gap (SQL-G15) with a committed minimal reproduction, not a ruling that the language lacks the construct — the construct is `CREATE SCHEMA`, it occurs 33 times in the pooled corpus, and the analyzer already builds both endpoint symbols.

decisions.question: AUTHORISED WORK — the lane census measures 0 `instantiates` edges in the 594-file duckdb corpus against 24 `cast` nodes carrying a `custom_type` FIELD. Is that a miss or is the D13 exclusion working?
decisions.resolution: RULED: THE EXCLUSION IS WORKING, the type is not under-delivering, and NO CODE CHANGED. The question was sized before the analyzer was touched, as authorised, by replaying the analyzer's own funnel over an independent full-tree walk. DUCKDB: of the 24 custom-type cast sites, 5 are a keyword/builtin target, 14 have an ERROR on the value side (DuckDB inline `STRUCT(...)` and a bracketed array literal - SQL-G17), 5 are conversions, and 0 are constructions. 0 edges is the correct output. POOLED: 184 custom-type sites -> 7 builtin, 14 damaged, 127 conversions, 36 constructions; the analyzer emits 21 edges, and those 36 sites sit in 17 distinct (file, target) pairs of which 0 has no edge. The 36 -> 21 difference is edge dedup on (type, source, target), and 21 > 17 because the source varies by statement: both are the intended semantics of a DEPENDENCY edge rather than a call-site record. The conversion bucket was audited for a hidden constructor, since `constructsAValue` accepts only a callee literally named `row`: the 8 invocation-valued conversions are `now()::wh_timestamp` and `xmlconcat2(...)::"text/xml"`, both conversions of an existing value. OVERTURN CONDITION: a `cast` whose target is a declared composite type, whose value side carries no ERROR and whose value is a `ROW(...)` invocation, a `list` or an `array`, that produces no `instantiates` edge at (file, target) granularity.

execute_literal_pass.decision: Recover DDL that a migration hands over as a string by SCANNING THE TEXT for `EXECUTE [IMMEDIATE] '<sql>'` and re-parsing each literal, rather than by extending the grammar to parse procedural bodies. Both were tried; the text route is what ships.
execute_literal_pass.why: A tree-sitter grammar parses one language and cannot produce `statement` nodes for SQL that is text inside a string literal. This was tested rather than assumed: the plpgsql grammar cut ProxiCall error nodes 36% and added 9% structure while leaving product output BYTE-IDENTICAL, because parsing the body still leaves the DDL inside a string. The text route needs no grammar change and therefore works on the grammar that is actually wired.
invariants: The RAW between-the-quotes slice is handed to the parser WITH its '' escapes intact, so every recovered range stays byte-exact; unescaping first would shift every range after the first escaped quote.
Comments and nested strings are skipped, so commented-out DDL cannot become a symbol. This is the pass's only false-positive path and it is pinned by a forbidSymbols row and its own mutant.
Dollar-quoted regions are deliberately NOT skipped — that is where these literals live.
The pass is strictly additive through the same declarationKeys the resync uses, and it reports executeLiterals / executeRecovered / executeSkipped in metadata.ambiguity.

harness_setGrammar.decision: script/m14/run-fixtures.ts now hands the parser's language to the analyzer's static setGrammar, mirroring script/m60/verify-sql-resync.ts, before running fixtures.
harness_setGrammar.why: The lane calls analyzer.analyze() directly, so the engine's setGrammar handoff in parseRaw never ran for it, and analyze is synchronous while Language.load is not. Every recovery pass was therefore INERT in the fixture lane. The cost was not theoretical: the resync could not be pinned by any synthetic fixture and needed its own corpus gate, and a mutant that deleted the EXECUTE pass 'passed' by never running. Two traps, both hit: setGrammar is STATIC so it must be reached through analyzer.constructor, and an ambiguity between two grammar rules is a reason to DECLARE the conflict, not to delete a capability.
